name: security-postfix
task_summary: Verify security remediation and audit new crypto layer

spawn_spec.prompt:
<review_type>SECURITY POST-FIX VERIFICATION - CROSS-CUTTING, READ-ONLY</review_type>

You are re-auditing EclipticRD (ultra-low latency macOS remote desktop, repo root /Users/indo/code/project/EclipticRD-Rewrite) after a security overhaul. The PREVIOUS audit found: unauthenticated remote input/screen control, no TLS/DTLS, public ntfy.sh with 6-digit PIN topics, silent clipboard exfiltration, unbounded audio buffer DoS, 4GB frame alloc amplification, no input rate limiting, allow-unsigned-executable-memory entitlement, public OSLog. Your job: (1) verify each is now remediated, (2) audit the NEW security layer itself for flaws (this is the most important part - fresh attack surface was added).

Claimed remediation (verify each in code):
- TLS-PSK on TCP (bootstrap PIN-derived PSK + host consent prompt + 5-attempt global lockout -> 256-bit Keychain pairing key for later sessions); UDP datagrams AES-256-GCM with direction keys (HKDF from pairing key + session salt), replay window
- Signaling: ntfy.sh topic = 256-bit HKDF hash of PIN, payloads AES-GCM encrypted
- Clipboard: concealed/transient pasteboard types skipped, 4KB cap
- Frame totalSize/chunks bounds; audio buffer size cap; input token-bucket rate limit + coordinate clamp
- Entitlement removed; info/debug/network logs private

NEW attack surface to audit hard:
- Sources/Shared/ERDCrypto.swift: HKDF implementation correctness, DatagramCipher nonce/replay-window logic (can an attacker desync the window? nonce collisions? AAD binding?)
- Sources/Shared/ERDIdentity.swift: PairingManager state machine (lockout bypass? PIN expiry races? Keychain usage), bootstrap identity flow
- Sources/Shared/PairingPayloads.swift + TCPChannel.ChannelSecurity + ServerCore.handlePairingRequest/handleClientHandshake + ClientCore pairing path: can an unpaired peer stream/input before approval? grant/replay confusion? handshake gating bypass?
- Sources/Shared/TCPChannel.swift ChannelSecurity.tlsParameters: PSK handling correctness
- project.yml + Sources/Resources/EclipticRD.entitlements: entitlement minimality

Read COMPLETELY: Sources/Shared/ERDCrypto.swift, ERDIdentity.swift, PairingPayloads.swift, TCPChannel.swift, UDPChannel.swift, FramePayloads.swift, SignalingClient.swift, ClipboardMonitor.swift; Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift, InputReceiver.swift; Sources/ClientCore/ClientCore.swift, InputSender.swift; Sources/Resources/EclipticRD.entitlements, project.yml.

RULES: READ-ONLY (no edits, no builds). Verify by reading code; no speculation. If you cannot read a file, say so.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
<verdict>PASS or FAIL</verdict>
<severity>CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NONE</severity>
<summary>2-4 sentences</summary>
<remediation_verification>per previous finding: REMEDIATED / PARTIAL / OPEN with file:line</remediation_verification>
<new_findings>
- [CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW] Category: description
  File: path:line
  Risk + Remediation
</new_findings>
<blocking_issues>CRITICAL+HIGH only</blocking_issues>

final_response:
<verdict>FAIL</verdict>
<severity>CRITICAL</severity>
<summary>
While previous architectural issues (clipboard leak, audio buffer DoS, frame allocation bounds, log privacy, and excessive entitlements) have been remediated, the newly introduced security layer contains critical flaws. Most severely, ServerCore fails to enforce session-state gating on TCP, allowing unapproved peers who connect via bootstrap PIN to bypass host consent prompts and inject input or stream video directly. Furthermore, the 5-attempt pairing lockout is dead code (allowing unthrottled PIN brute force), and an unchecked integer addition in DatagramCipher allows unauthenticated remote crash DoS via UDP.
</summary>

<remediation_verification>
- TLS-PSK on TCP & AES-256-GCM UDP ciphers: PARTIAL (Sources/Shared/TCPChannel.swift:15, Sources/Shared/ERDCrypto.swift:42) — TLS 1.3 PSK and AES-256-GCM ciphers are implemented, but UDPChannel silently falls back to plaintext if ciphers are unset (Sources/Shared/UDPChannel.swift:98, 173), and ServerCore lacks session-state gating (Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift:67).
- Pairing PIN consent prompt & 5-attempt lockout: PARTIAL (Sources/Shared/ERDIdentity.swift:181, Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift:67) — Host consent prompt exists, but unapproved clients can bypass it by sending stream/input packets directly. `recordBootstrapFailure()` is never called anywhere in the codebase.
- Signaling ntfy.sh 256-bit HKDF topic & AES-GCM payloads: REMEDIATED (Sources/Shared/SignalingClient.swift:23-35) — Topics are derived via 256-bit HKDF SHA-256 hash of PIN; candidates are AES-256-GCM encrypted.
- Clipboard concealed/transient suppression & 4KB limit: REMEDIATED (Sources/Shared/ClipboardMonitor.swift:16-19, 94-106) — `org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType` and `TransientType` are rejected; payload capped at 4096 bytes.
- Unbounded audio buffer DoS: REMEDIATED (Sources/ClientCore/ClientAudioPlayer.swift:54, 40-42) — Buffer size capped at 64KB (65,536 bytes); buffers freed deterministically via `AudioQueueFreeBuffer`.
- 4GB frame alloc amplification bounds: REMEDIATED (Sources/Shared/FramePayloads.swift:34, Sources/ClientCore/FrameReceiver.swift:115) — Frame sizes capped at 32 MiB (`maxFrameBytes`), chunks at 1024 (`maxChunksPerFrame`), and orphan chunk queue capped.
- Input token-bucket rate limit & coordinate clamp: REMEDIATED (Sources/HostCore/InputReceiver.swift:22-26, 68-78) — Coordinates clamped to `[0, 1]`; token-bucket rate limits to 200 events/s with 400 burst capacity.
- Entitlement minimality: REMEDIATED (Sources/Resources/EclipticRD.entitlements:1-8, project.yml:32) — `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` removed; hardened runtime enabled.
- OSLog privacy: REMEDIATED (Sources/Shared/ERDLog.swift:20, 29, 39) — `info`, `debug`, and `network` logs use `%{private}@`.
</remediation_verification>

<new_findings>
- [CRITICAL] Authentication / Authorization: Host Consent Prompt & Session Gating Bypass
  File: Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift:67-106
  Risk: When a client connects over TCP using the temporary bootstrap PIN, `ServerCore.tcpChannel.onReceive` handles `.inputEvent` and `.control` (`.startStream`, `.streamConfigRequest`, `.requestKeyFrame`) without validating if the connection is authenticated or approved. A malicious client knowing the temporary PIN can immediately start video capture and inject synthetic keyboard/mouse events into the macOS HID system without triggering `onPairingRequest` and without host user approval.
  Remediation: Implement a connection state machine (`unauthenticated`, `pairingPending`, `authenticated`). Bootstrap connections (`erd-b1`) must be restricted exclusively to `.pairingRequest` until the host user explicitly accepts the prompt and a pairing key is granted. Reject `.inputEvent`, `.control`, and stream initialization on unapproved connections.

- [HIGH] Authentication: Dead Code Lockout Permitting Unthrottled Bootstrap PIN Brute-Force
  File: Sources/Shared/ERDIdentity.swift:181-193, Sources/Shared/TCPChannel.swift:15-30
  Risk: `PairingManager.recordBootstrapFailure()` is never invoked anywhere in the codebase. When a client attempts invalid PSKs against `NWListener`, Network.framework drops the connection at the TLS handshake layer without notifying `PairingManager`. As a result, the claimed 5-attempt global lockout is inactive, enabling attackers on LAN or low-latency networks to brute-force the 8-digit PIN without rate limits.
  Remediation: Hook TLS handshake failures in `TCPChannel` to call `PairingManager.shared.recordBootstrapFailure()`, and dynamically revoke/remove the bootstrap PSK from `NWListener` when lockout is active.

- [HIGH] Denial of Service: Remote DoS via Integer Overflow in DatagramCipher Replay Window
  File: Sources/Shared/ERDCrypto.swift:76
  Risk: In `DatagramCipher.open()`, the replay window check executes `guard counter + Self.windowSize > highestReceived else { return nil }` using standard unchecked `UInt64` addition. An unauthenticated attacker sending a UDP datagram to port 19731 with packet counter bytes set to `>= UInt64.max - 4096` causes a Swift arithmetic overflow runtime trap, crashing the host or client application immediately.
  Remediation: Replace unchecked addition with safe comparison arithmetic:
  `guard highestReceived <= counter || highestReceived - counter < Self.windowSize else { return nil }`

- [MEDIUM] Cryptography: Silent Fallback to Plaintext UDP Datagrams
  File: Sources/Shared/UDPChannel.swift:92-100, 172-181
  Risk: `UDPChannel.sendPacket` and `UDPChannel.decodeDatagram` fall back to sending and receiving unencrypted plaintext packets when `sendCipher` / `receiveCipher` is `nil`. If streaming begins before cipher keys are derived, video frames and cursor positions are transmitted over the network in cleartext.
  Remediation: Require encryption unconditionally in `UDPChannel`. Discard any outbound or inbound packets if ciphers are not initialized.

- [LOW] Cryptography: Unverified Binding Between TLS PSK Identity and Handshake Pairing ID
  File: Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift:274-297, Sources/Shared/TCPChannel.swift:15-30
  Risk: In `handleClientHandshake`, `ServerCore` loads the pairing key using the application-layer `hs.pairingID` string without validating that the underlying TLS 1.3 session negotiated that specific PSK identity.
  Remediation: Query `sec_protocol_metadata_t` on the connection to ensure the negotiated TLS PSK identity matches `erd-p1.\(hs.pairingID)`.
</new_findings>

<blocking_issues>
- CRITICAL: Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift:67 — Missing connection state gating allows bootstrap connections to bypass host approval prompt and execute arbitrary remote input/streaming.
- HIGH: Sources/Shared/ERDIdentity.swift:181 — `recordBootstrapFailure()` is dead code, allowing unthrottled TLS-PSK PIN brute-forcing.
- HIGH: Sources/Shared/ERDCrypto.swift:76 — Integer overflow in `DatagramCipher.open` enables remote crash DoS via UDP.
</blocking_issues>
